mainTopic: The laws of פסין around a well: courtyards that open into them, water that dries up or returns on שבת, and the strength of partitions even when crowds pass through.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a rejection of a proof from a ברייתא: a fence listed twice means two types of fence, just as a tree listed twice means two types of tree. אביי then asks רבה about a חצר that opens into the area between the פסין around a well. רבה rules that one חצר may carry there but two courtyards may not. רב הונא forbids two courtyards even with an עירוב, as a גזירה, while רבא permits them with an עירוב. A ברייתא supports רבא, and the גמרא defends רב הונא by saying the ברייתא is about courtyards that physically became one. Next, רבה rules that if the well dries up on שבת the פסין stop working. אביי adds that if the water returns on שבת, they work again, because a partition made on שבת still counts; only if someone built it on purpose is carrying inside it forbidden. רבי אלעזר rules that throwing into פסי ביראות makes one חייב, which teaches that a partition still counts even when crowds walk through it. The amud ends by starting a new section on the משנה's words 'מותר להקריב לבאר', comparing the rule that a person drinking across רשויות must bring his head and most of his body inside.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: two types of fence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting a proof from a ברייתא. The ברייתא's double mention of a fence can be read as two types of fence, just as its double mention of a tree is read as two types of tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't we say the ברייתא is teaching two kinds of tree? Here too, it is teaching two kinds of fence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion by knocking down a proof that someone tried to bring from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone wanted to learn something from the fact that the ברייתא lists a fence twice. The answer is that the ברייתא also lists a tree twice, and everyone agrees that means two different kinds of tree. In the same way, the double fence just means two kinds of fence, so nothing new can be proven from it.
steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence that began on the previous עמוד. It is the end of a rejection, not the start of a new topic.

phrases.english: [Don't you say it means] two types of tree?
phrases.notes: The listing that everyone already accepts is used as a model.

phrases.english: Here too, [it means] two types of fence.
phrases.notes: So the extra mention of a fence proves nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous (unseen) proof attempt by rejecting it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof drawn from the ברייתא's double mention of a fence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The repetition is explained as two types of fence, the same way the repeated tree is explained, so it carries no extra חידוש.

steps.title: אביי asks about a courtyard opening into the area of the boards
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה whether one may carry between a חצר and the area enclosed by פסין when the חצר's open end extends into that area.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: a חצר whose open end goes into the area between the פסין — may one carry from inside the חצר to the area between the פסין, and from the area between the פסין into the חצר?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. אביי asks whether a חצר and the area enclosed by פסין count as one space for carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסין are corner boards placed around a well in a public area. They are a special leniency so that the enclosed space counts as a private domain, mainly for watering animals. The question is whether a regular חצר that opens into this enclosed space may share carrying with it.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked of him (a sincere question)
the area enclosed by the boards around a well
to carry / move objects on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rabba:
A courtyard whose [open] end enters between the boards —
phrases.notes: The open side of the courtyard extends into the enclosed area.

phrases.english: what is [the law] about carrying from inside it to between the boards,
and from between the boards into it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new inquiry by אביי, separate from the fence discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may carry between a single חצר and the area between the פסין when the חצר opens into it.

steps.title: רבה: one courtyard is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that carrying between one חצר and the area between the פסין is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's question with a simple ruling: it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one חצר, the same residents use both the חצר and the enclosed area. Nobody else shares the space, so they are treated as one area for carrying.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Carrying between one חצר and the area between the פסין is permitted.

steps.title: אביי asks about two courtyards
steps.stepSummary: אביי follows up: what is the law if two courtyards open into the area between the פסין?
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are two courtyards, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes further and asks about a case with two courtyards instead of one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-חצר case was easy because only one group of residents was involved. Now two separate groups of residents share the enclosed area, and that could create a problem.

phrases.english: Two [courtyards] — what [is the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the case from step 2 to two courtyards.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether carrying between the area between the פסין and two courtyards that open into it is permitted.

steps.title: רבה: two courtyards are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that with two courtyards, carrying is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rules that the two-חצר case is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two separate groups of residents both use the enclosed area, it becomes a shared space between them. Shared space between different households cannot simply be carried into, so the ruling flips from permitted to forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: One חצר opening into the area between the פסין = permitted. Two courtyards = forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With two courtyards, carrying to and from the area between the פסין is forbidden.

steps.title: רב הונא: forbidden even with an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that two courtyards stay forbidden even if they made an עירוב together. This is a גזירה so that people will not think an עירוב is what makes the area between the פסין usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Two courtyards are forbidden, even if they made an עירוב. This is a גזירה, lest people say, 'An עירוב works for the area between the פסין.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains how far רבה's prohibition reaches: even an עירוב between the two courtyards does not permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עירוב joins two courtyards into one, so we might expect it to solve the problem. רב הונא forbids it anyway as a rabbinic safeguard. The concern is that people might think the עירוב is what permits the area between the פסין, when the פסין are really a special, limited leniency for wells.

keyTerms.meaning: they made an עירוב (joined their domains)
a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not say an עירוב fails to join two courtyards in general. He forbids this one case as a safeguard, so that people will not misunderstand how the פסין work.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Two [courtyards] are forbidden, and even if they made an eiruv.
[It is] a decree, lest they say
"An eiruv is effective for the area between the boards."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שְׁתַּיִם אֲסוּרִין, וַאֲפִילּוּ עֵירְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבה's prohibition on two courtyards to include the case where they made an עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two courtyards that open into the area between the פסין are forbidden even with an עירוב, as a גזירה.

steps.title: רבא: with an עירוב it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רב הונא and rules that if the two courtyards made an עירוב, carrying is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If they made an עירוב, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposing view: the עירוב solves the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the עירוב turns the two courtyards into one group of residents. That brings the case back to the permitted one-חצר case of step 3. He does not accept רב הונא's גזירה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: two courtyards are forbidden even with an עירוב (גזירה). רבא: with an עירוב they are permitted, because they count as one חצר.

phrases.english: Rava said: [If] they made an eiruv, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two courtyards that made an עירוב may carry to and from the area between the פסין.

steps.title: אביי brings a ברייתא that supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבא that a ברייתא supports his ruling. Two courtyards that made an עירוב together may carry into the area between the פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: A ברייתא supports you. A courtyard with one end opening into the area between the פסין may carry from the courtyard into that area, and from that area into the courtyard. With two courtyards, it is forbidden. When does this apply? When they did not make an עירוב together. If they did make an עירוב, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to back up רבא's opinion from Step 7. The ברייתא says that two courtyards that made an עירוב together may carry into the area between the פסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא matches what רבה said in Steps 3 and 5: one courtyard is permitted, and two courtyards are forbidden. The new information is the last line, which says the 'two is forbidden' rule only applies without an עירוב. That is exactly רבא's position.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (an outside teaching of the תנאים)
The area between the פסין, the corner boards set up around a well
In what case were these words said? (This phrase limits the rule that came before it)
They made an עירוב, which joins separate households so they may carry together

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
It was taught in a baraita that supports you
A courtyard, one end of which
enters into the area between the boards
it is permitted to carry from inside it to the area between the boards
and from between the boards into it
but with two courtyards, it is forbidden.
In what case were these words said?
Where they did not make an eruv;
but if they made an eruv, they are permitted.
phrases.notes: This line is the actual support for רבא

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: תַּנְיָא דִּמְסַיַּיע לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רבא's ruling from Step 7
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that two courtyards that made an עירוב may carry into the area between the פסין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly permits carrying for two courtyards that made an עירוב

steps.title: Does this ברייתא refute רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא is a refutation of רב הונא, who forbids carrying even with an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the ברייתא against רב הונא. If a ברייתא permits carrying with an עירוב, how can רב הונא forbid it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא like רב הונא cannot argue against a clear ברייתא. Since the ברייתא appears to say the opposite of his ruling in Step 6, his position seems to be in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a strong challenge from a source

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Huna?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 8 as a challenge against רב הונא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits carrying when there is an עירוב, which directly contradicts רב הונא's גזירה forbidding it

steps.title: רב הונא explains the ברייתא as a case of joined courtyards
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא could answer that the ברייתא is talking about two courtyards that later became joined into one courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא could say to you: There, the case is where the courtyards later became joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. It says the ברייתא is talking about a special case where the two courtyards later became joined, for example because the wall between them broke down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the two courtyards are clearly one, nobody will think that an עירוב is what makes the area between the פסין usable. Since that fear was the whole reason for רב הונא's גזירה, there is no reason to forbid in this case. His ruling still stands for two separate courtyards that only made an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (introduces a defense of someone's opinion)
There, meaning in the case of the ברייתא
They later became joined, so the two courtyards became one

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'וְעָרְבָן' does not mean they made an ordinary עירוב of food. It means the two courtyards physically became one, which is the opposite of the case רב הונא forbids.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives the challenge. The ברייתא permits only when the courtyards became physically joined, so his גזירה still applies to two separate courtyards that merely made an עירוב.

phrases.english: Rav Huna could say to you:
There, it is where they later became joined.
phrases.notes: For example, the dividing wall broke down and the two courtyards became one

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא permits any two courtyards that made a regular עירוב, which would contradict רב הונא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about courtyards that later became physically one, so the reason for רב הונא's גזירה does not apply there

steps.title: What if the well's water dries up on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה what the law is if the water in the well dries up on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: If the water dried up on שבת, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the פסין. אביי asks whether people may still carry between the פסין if the water dries up during שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסין are allowed in the first place only so that people can get water. The question is whether the enclosure stays valid for the rest of שבת once the water is gone, since it was valid when שבת began.

phrases.english: Abaye asked of Rabba:
If the water dried up on Shabbat, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the פסין, separate from the courtyard discussion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פסין remain a valid enclosure after the water dries up on שבת

steps.title: No water means no partition
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the פסין count as a מחיצה only because of the water. Without water, there is no מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The partition was made only because of the water. If there is no water here, there is no partition here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי. Once the water is gone, the פסין stop working and carrying is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסין are a weak partition that חז"ל allowed only for the sake of getting water. Since the reason for allowing them was the water, the allowance ends as soon as the water is gone, even in the middle of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Was it at all...? (a rhetorical opening meaning 'only')
For the sake of, because of

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: the validity of the פסין depends on the water being there, not only on the boards.

phrases.english: He said to him: Was it made a partition at all
except because of the water?
Water is not here,
so a partition is not here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלוּם נַעֲשֵׂית מְחִיצָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Carrying is forbidden, because the פסין only work as a מחיצה when there is water

steps.title: What if the water dries up and then returns on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבין asks about water that dries up on שבת and then comes back on the same שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין asked: If the water dried up on שבת and came back on שבת, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבין asks a follow-up question. If the water comes back later on the same שבת, does the permission to carry come back too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 already established that the פסין stop working once the water is gone. רבין's question is whether the returning water can make the enclosure work again in the middle of שבת.

phrases.english: Ravin asked:
If the water dried up on Shabbat
and came back on Shabbat, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבִין: יָבְשׁוּ מַיִם בְּשַׁבָּת וּבָאוּ בְּשַׁבָּת מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבה's ruling by adding the case of the water returning
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the permission to carry comes back when the water returns on the same שבת

steps.title: אביי says the drying-up part is already settled
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבין that the case of water drying up on שבת is not a question, because רבה already ruled that it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The case where the water dried up on שבת should not be a question for you. I already asked my master about it, and he ruled for me that it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins his reply by setting aside the first half of רבין's question. The drying-up case was already decided by רבה in Step 12, so this step is preparing to narrow the discussion to the case of the water coming back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי points out that one part of רבין's question was already answered: once the water dries up, carrying is forbidden. That leaves only the new element, the water returning, which אביי addresses in the next step (Step 15).

keyTerms.meaning: Do not ask about this; it is not a real question for you
Master (here referring to רבה, אביי's teacher)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Do not ask about where it dried up on Shabbat,
for I asked my Master about it
and he resolved for me that it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: יָבְשׁוּ בְּשַׁבָּת לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבין's question by pointing back to רבה's ruling in Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Water drying up on שבת makes carrying forbidden, as רבה already ruled. The discussion continues next.

steps.title: Water that comes back on שבת makes a valid partition again
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבין that the case where the water returns is also not a real question. A מחיצה that comes into being on שבת, in any way at all, still counts as a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case where the water came back should also not be a question for you. It is a partition made on שבת, and a ברייתא teaches: any partition made on שבת, whether by mistake or on purpose, whether by accident or willingly, is called a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer to רבין. If the water dries up and then comes back on the same שבת, the פסין count as a מחיצה again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסין only work as a מחיצה because of the water. So when the water returns, it is as if a new partition was made right now, on שבת. The ברייתא says a partition made on שבת still counts, no matter how it was made. So carrying there is allowed again.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that was made (came into being) on שבת
It was taught in a ברייתא
By accident or force, not by anyone's choice

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two cases up. Water that dried up on שבת means NO מחיצה, so carrying is forbidden (step 14). Water that came back on שבת means the מחיצה works again (this step).

phrases.english: If the water came back, this also should not be a question for you
phrases.notes: The water dried up and then returned on the same שבת

phrases.english: because it is a partition made on שבת
and it was taught: any partition made on שבת,
whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether by accident or willingly,
it is called a partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer to רבין's question. Step 14 dealt with the drying up; this step deals with the water returning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law if the water dried up on שבת and then came back on the same שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסין work again as a מחיצה, because a partition made on שבת still counts, in any manner.

steps.title: רב נחמן limits the rule to throwing, not carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבין objects. רב נחמן said the ברייתא only means the partition counts to make one חייב for throwing. It does not mean you may carry inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this ברייתא that רב נחמן said: they only taught this for throwing, but for carrying, no?
steps.whatsHappening: רבין challenges אביי. According to רב נחמן, a partition made on שבת does not make it permitted to carry inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי used the ברייתא to show that carrying is allowed once the water returns. רב נחמן reads the ברייתא as a חומרא only: the area counts as private when it comes to throwing in from outside, but carrying inside it stays forbidden. If so, the returning water would not permit carrying at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said about it (an אמורא's comment on an earlier source)
They only taught this for..., a phrase that limits a source
To throw, from one domain into another
To carry or move objects within the area

phrases.english: But was it not said about it,
that רב נחמן said:
They taught this only for throwing,
phrases.notes: For throwing, it counts as a real partition, so one is חייב

phrases.english: but to carry inside it, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא that אביי relied on in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's conclusion that carrying is permitted once the water returns on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן limited the ברייתא to throwing and excluded carrying. So a partition made on שבת cannot permit carrying.

steps.title: רב נחמן spoke only about a partition made on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's limit applies only to a partition someone put up on purpose (מזיד). Water returning by itself is not that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב נחמן's statement was said, it was said about a partition made on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. רב נחמן's limit does not apply to water that returned on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who builds a partition on שבת on purpose is penalized, so carrying inside it is forbidden. A partition that formed by mistake, or by itself like returning water, gets no such penalty. So carrying is allowed there, and אביי's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: When it was said..., a phrase that narrows the scope of an earlier statement
A rabbinic penalty, here against someone who built on purpose on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: A מחיצה made on שבת always counts for throwing. Carrying inside is forbidden only when it was made on purpose (מזיד). When it formed by mistake or by itself, carrying is allowed.

phrases.english: When רב נחמן's statement was said,
it was said about a partition made on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב נַחְמָן אַמֵּזִיד אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by narrowing רב נחמן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן forbids carrying in every partition made on שבת, including water that returned by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן forbids carrying only where the partition was made on purpose, as a penalty. Water that returns by itself is fine for carrying.

steps.title: Throwing into the area between the well boards makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that someone who throws from the public domain into the area between the פסי ביראות is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: One who throws into the area between the boards of the wells is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי אלעזר. The area between the פסין counts as a full private domain, so throwing into it is a real Torah-level violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This treats the פסין as a true מחיצה on a Torah level, not just a rabbinic leniency. Throwing from the public domain into a real private domain is a מלאכה that makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: The upright corner boards placed around wells
Liable, here to bring a קרבן חטאת

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
One who throws into the area between the well boards is liable.
phrases.notes: Throwing from the public domain into the enclosed area

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַזּוֹרֵק לְבֵין פַּסֵּי הַבֵּירָאוֹת חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement about the פסין, moving from carrying inside to throwing in from outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing from the public domain into the area between the פסי ביראות makes one חייב.

steps.title: Why does רבי אלעזר need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר's ruling is needed. If the area were not a real private domain, how could anyone be allowed to draw water there?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! If it were not a partition, how would he be allowed to draw water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's statement as too obvious to need saying. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know people may draw water and carry it inside the פסין. That only works if the area is a real private domain. So of course throwing into it makes one חייב. What new thing is רבי אלעזר teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new
To draw water and fill containers

phrases.english: It is obvious!
If it were not a valid partition,
how would he be permitted to draw water?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 18 as obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי אלעזר's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since drawing water inside the פסין is allowed, the area must already be a full private domain. So liability for throwing in follows automatically, and the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Boards like פסי ביראות set up in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where someone puts up boards like פסי ביראות in רשות הרבים, with no well, and throws into them. He is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed for a case where a person made something like the boards around wells in the public domain and threw an object into it. He is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19 by saying what new case רבי אלעזר is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the גמרא said the area by a real well must be a private domain, or drawing water there would be forbidden. Now it moves the ruling to a different case: boards set up like פסי ביראות where there is no well. The point would be that the boards make a private domain even without a well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (introduces the special case a ruling is teaching)
Corner boards placed around a well so people may draw water on שבת

phrases.english: It is only necessary
where he made something like the boards around wells
phrases.notes: Boards set up without a real well.

phrases.english: in the public domain
and threw into it — he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דַּעֲבַד כְּעֵין פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why is this needed' question of Step 19 by moving the ruling to a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the ruling to a narrower, new case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ruling seemed obvious about a real well area.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches that boards like פסי ביראות with no well still make a private domain for throwing.

steps.title: This is also obvious, because carrying by a cistern depends on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: this is also obvious. If such boards were not a real מחיצה in general, how could anyone carry near a cistern?
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious! If it were not a partition in general, how could he be allowed to carry by a cistern?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of Step 20 and says the new case is also obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being allowed to carry by a בור shows that these boards work as a real מחיצה. If they work as a מחיצה there, they should also work in רשות הרבים. So saying it again teaches nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (a challenge: why say it at all?)
Cistern, a pit that holds water

phrases.english: This too is obvious!
If it were not a partition in general,
regarding a cistern
how would he be permitted to carry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 20 as also being obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ruling is about boards set up in רשות הרבים without a well
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying by a cistern is only allowed because these boards are a real מחיצה, so they must be a מחיצה everywhere. Teaching it again adds nothing.

steps.title: It counts even though many people walk through it
steps.stepSummary: The new point is that the boards count as a מחיצה even though many people pass through the open gaps.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed to teach that it counts even though many people pass through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 21 by finding a new detail that makes רבי אלעזר's ruling needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסי ביראות are only corner boards, so the sides are wide open and crowds walk right through. You might think people walking through ruins the partition. רבי אלעזר teaches that it still counts, so throwing into it from outside makes one חייב.

phrases.english: It is only necessary
even though
many people pass through it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא בָּקְעִי בָּהּ רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by pointing to a new detail: crowds walking through.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a new detail to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that crowds walking through the gaps cancel the partition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with crowds passing through, the boards remain a valid מחיצה, so one who throws in is חייב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main idea of the passage: a halachic partition does not need to block people physically to count.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר already taught this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the point is that crowds do not cancel a מחיצה, רבי אלעזר already said that once.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does he teach us, that the many do not come and cancel the partition? But רבי אלעזר already said this once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 22. רבי אלעזר would be repeating himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea, that people passing through do not cancel a מחיצה, is not new at all. רבי אלעזר already stated it somewhere else. An אמורא does not usually say the same rule twice, so the answer seems weak. The next step gives the earlier source.

phrases.english: And what does he teach us?
That the many do not come
and cancel the partition?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֲמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Elazar already said it once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 22 because it makes רבי אלעזר repeat himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי אלעזר teaches that crowds do not cancel a partition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר already stated this exact idea elsewhere. A second statement would add nothing.

steps.title: The earlier source: the power of partitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where רבי יהודה says a public path through פסי ביראות must be moved and the חכמים disagree. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר said this shows the strength of partitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה says, if a public path cuts through them, he must move it to the sides. The חכמים say he does not need to. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both said: here it shows you the power of partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim of Step 23 by quoting where רבי אלעזר already taught this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a public path cutting through the boards ruins them, so it must be moved away. The חכמים say this is not needed, so the boards work even with crowds passing through. Since רבי אלעזר explained the חכמים as showing 'the power of partitions,' he already taught that crowds do not cancel a מחיצה. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
He must move it (the path) to the sides

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. It is the proof behind the challenge in Step 23, showing that רבי אלעזר already said this. Step 25 answers the challenge.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If there was a public path
cutting through them,
he must move it to the sides.
And the Sages say: he does not need to.
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar
who both said:
Here it informed you of the power of partitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that supports the challenge of Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי אלעזר already taught that crowds do not cancel a partition
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a public path through פסי ביראות, with רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר's comment 'כאן הודיעך כחן של מחיצות'

steps.title: The earlier statement alone would not show that רבי אלעזר agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question of step 23. From רבי אלעזר's comment on the משנה alone, we might think he was only explaining the חכמים' view without agreeing with it. His ruling about throwing shows that he agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the statement from there, I would have said that 'here' the חכמים taught the strength of partitions, but רבי אלעזר himself does not hold that way. So he teaches us that 'here' they taught it, and he does hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אלעזר's ruling about throwing into the boards is not just a repeat of his earlier statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's comment 'כאן הודיעך כחן של מחיצות' could be read as simply describing the חכמים' opinion in the משנה. That reading leaves open whether he agrees, since רבי יהודה disagrees there. His ruling that a thrower is חייב shows that he personally holds that the boards are a real מחיצה even with crowds passing through.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were only from there (from the other source)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'כאן' ('here') is quoted from רבי אלעזר's earlier comment, 'כאן הודיעך כחן של מחיצות'. It is not a new statement in this line.

phrases.english: If it were only from there (the earlier statement),
I would have said: 'here' (the חכמים taught the strength of partitions)
phrases.notes: Quoting רבי אלעזר's comment on the משנה

phrases.english: but he himself does not hold that way.
So it teaches us: 'here' (they taught it)
and he does hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23, using the source brought in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: The second statement reveals רבי אלעזר's personal opinion, which the first statement left unclear
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר was only explaining the חכמים' view and did not agree with it
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר agrees that the boards are a real מחיצה despite crowds passing, so a thrower is חייב

steps.title: Then why not say only the throwing ruling?
steps.stepSummary: If the throwing ruling shows everything, רבי אלעזר should have said just that one, and the other comment would not be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him say this one, and he would not need that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks from the other side. If the throwing ruling already teaches the whole point, why did רבי אלעזר also make the comment on the משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The throwing ruling already shows that partitions are strong and that רבי אלעזר agrees. That makes the comment 'כאן הודיעך כחן של מחיצות' look extra. The question is why a sage would say two statements when one is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: And he would not need that one

phrases.english: So let him say this (the throwing ruling),
and he would not need that (the other comment)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 25 by turning it around
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי אלעזר's comment 'כאן הודיעך כחן של מחיצות'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the throwing ruling teaches everything, the second statement adds nothing

steps.title: Only one statement was said; the other was learned from it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר really made only one statement. His students drew the second one from it and reported it in his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was said by inference from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there were not really two separate statements. One was said, and the other was understood from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר did not repeat himself. He said one of the rulings directly, and the other was a logical conclusion drawn from it. That is why it was passed down as a separate saying. With this answer, the discussion about רבי אלעזר is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: One was stated by inference from the other

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר holds that פסי ביראות are a real מחיצה even when crowds pass through. Someone who throws into them from רשות הרבים is חייב. His two 'statements' are really one statement plus a conclusion drawn from it.

phrases.english: One was stated by inference from the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the redundancy: only one statement was actually said
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר made two separate, overlapping statements
steps.terutzMaskana: He said one, and the other was derived from it by his students

steps.title: A new phrase from the משנה, paired with the rule of drinking across רשויות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'מותר להקריב לבאר' from our משנה. It then brings another משנה: a person may not stand in one רשות and drink in another unless his head and most of his body enter the place where he drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted to bring the boards closer to the well, etc. We learned there: A person may not stand in רשות הרבים and drink in רשות היחיד, or stand in רשות היחיד and drink in רשות הרבים, unless he brings his head and most of his body into the place where he is drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section on our משנה's words 'מותר להקריב לבאר'. It quotes another משנה to set up the next move, which is a comparison with the cow drinking with 'its head and most of its body' inside the boards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lets the boards be moved closer to the well, as long as a cow's head and most of its body fit inside the enclosed area. The other משנה gives a similar measure for a person, who must bring his head and most of his body into the רשות where he drinks. Placing the two side by side prepares a discussion of how the two rules relate.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring the boards closer to the well
We learned in a משנה elsewhere
His head and most of his body

steps.whyThisMatters: The 'head and most of the body' measure appears both for a person and for an animal. It is the key to deciding how small the enclosed area around the well may be.

phrases.english: 'It is permitted to bring (the boards) closer to the well,' etc.
We learned there (in another משנה):
A person may not stand in a public domain
and drink in a private domain,
(or stand) in a private domain and drink in a public domain,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ
phrases.english: unless he brings his head and most of his body
into the place where he is drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after the discussion of רבי אלעזר ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may not drink across רשויות unless his head and most of his body are in the רשות where he drinks
